title: Hydrolysis-Promoted Building Block Assembly: Structure Transformation from Y12 Wheel and Y34 Ship to Y60 Cage

synthesis.procedure: Prepared by reacting a yttrium(III) salt with 2,2-dimethylolpropionic acid in the presence of triethanolamine at pH 4. The article states that either yttrium perchlorate or yttrium nitrate can yield the Y12 cluster, but does not give reagent quantities in the main text.

reagents.name: yttrium(III) perchlorate
reagents.amount: 4 mL of a 1.0 M aqueous solution

synthesis.time: 2 h heating and stirring; crystals appeared after about one month
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Filtered, then left to cool to room temperature; colorless crystals appeared after about one month.

source_locations.location: paragraph introducing Y12, Y34, and Y60; Scheme 1

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: Four vertex-sharing cubane-like [Y4(μ3-OH)4] units form a 12-yttrium [Y12(μ3-OH)16] wheel, protected by eight dmpa ligands and twelve coordinated water molecules.

synthesis.procedure: Prepared by a method similar to that used for Y12, but at pH 5, using yttrium(III) perchlorate with 2,2-dimethylolpropionic acid in the presence of triethanolamine. Carbonate in the product arises from fixation of atmospheric CO2. The main text does not provide reagent quantities.

reagents.name: yttrium(III) perchlorate
reagents.amount: 4 mL of a 1.0 M aqueous solution

synthesis.time: 2 h heating and stirring; crystals obtained after about one month
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Filtered, then left to cool to room temperature; colorless crystals were obtained after about one month.

source_locations.location: paragraph introducing Y12, Y34, and Y60; Y34 structural discussion

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: Twelve cubane-like [Y4(μ3-OH)4] motifs form a ship-like 34-yttrium core. Two carbonate-templated Y18 hexagonal wheels are joined through shared cubane vertices and carbonate bridges; the core is stabilized by 27 dmpa ligands and twelve terminal water ligands.

synthesis.procedure: Obtained by hydrolysis of yttrium(III) nitrate with 2,2-dimethylolpropionic acid in the presence of triethanolamine at pH 6. The article also reports transformation of Y12 or Y34: an ethanol solution of either cluster was mixed with aqueous yttrium(III) nitrate solution at approximately pH 3, heated for 2 h, and Y60 crystals formed after 2 weeks. Neither preparation has a numerical reagent amount in the main text.

reagents.name: yttrium(III) nitrate hexahydrate
reagents.amount: 4 mL of a 1.0 M aqueous solution

synthesis.temperature: heated (temperature not specified) in the transformation
synthesis.time: 2 h heating; crystals after 2 weeks in the transformation
synthesis.ph: 6 in direct synthesis; approximately 3 for the aqueous yttrium nitrate solution in the transformation
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: Y60 crystals obtained after 2 weeks in the transformation

list_of_rare_earth_compounds.structure_description: Twenty-four vertex-sharing cubane-like [Y4(μ3-OH)4] motifs form a sodalite-topology cage with six square and eight hexagonal faces. Each hexagon contains a carbonate template. The core can be viewed structurally as six vertex-connected Y12 units or two vertex-connected Y34 units; this decomposition does not establish either as an observed intermediate in the direct synthesis.
